mean: to stake everything on one last gamble
lit: to throw the last stake in a single cast of the dice

story.text: In gambling, a player who had nearly lost everything and pushed all he had left onto the table was said to make a 'lone stake' (guzhu), his last one. In the Song dynasty, the official Wang Qinruo told Emperor Zhenzong that when the minister Kou Zhun urged him to go to the front at Chanyuan, Kou Zhun had used the emperor himself as his last stake. The emperor's favour towards Kou Zhun cooled after this.

use.how: Predicate or adverbial, often with 决定 or 只好: 他决定孤注一掷。 Said of a risky all-or-nothing move made when other options are gone; often slightly critical.

near.diff: 破釜沉舟 praises cutting off one's own retreat to fight with total resolve; 孤注一掷 stresses betting everything on one risky chance.

cue: Down to his last savings, a man puts every cent into one risky venture: if it fails, he has nothing left. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 他把全部积蓄都拿去开店，真是{孤注一掷}。
ctx.en: He put all his savings into opening a shop: a real all-or-nothing bet.

ctx.s: 比赛只剩最后一分钟，教练决定{孤注一掷}，让守门员也上前进攻。
ctx.en: With one minute left, the coach decided to go for broke and sent even the goalkeeper forward.

ctx.s: “你真要把房子卖了去创业？”“没别的办法了，只能{孤注一掷}。”
ctx.en: "You're really selling the house to start a business?" "There's no other way; I have to risk it all."

ctx.s: 公司濒临破产，老板{孤注一掷}，把最后的资金全部投进了新产品。
ctx.en: With the company near bankruptcy, the boss staked everything, pouring the last of the money into a new product.

ctx.s: 投资需要冷静，千万不要在亏损之后{孤注一掷}。
ctx.en: Investing needs a cool head; never bet everything on one throw after a loss.

ctx.s: 敌军被围多日，粮草将尽，终于{孤注一掷}，趁夜突围。
ctx.en: Surrounded for days and almost out of supplies, the enemy finally made a desperate all-out bid to break out by night.

bad.s: 我周末{孤注一掷}，去看了一场电影。
bad.en: (meant: I decided on a whim to see a film at the weekend)
bad.why: It means risking everything one has on one chance; seeing a film risks nothing.

bad.s: 他学习很稳定，每次考试都{孤注一掷}地拿高分。
bad.en: (meant: he steadily gets high marks in every exam)
bad.why: It describes a desperate one-off gamble, not steady, reliable success.

mean: to believe firmly without a doubt
lit: to believe deeply and not doubt

use.how: Predicate, usually with 对……深信不疑 or followed by a clause: 他对这件事深信不疑。 Said of a person's belief in a claim, a person or an idea, true or false.

near.diff: 信以为真 is taking something false to be true, usually a trick or rumour; 深信不疑 is just firm belief, which may well be right.

cue: Everyone tells her the plan won't work, but she has no doubt at all that it will. How would you describe her belief?

ctx.s: 孩子们对圣诞老人的存在{深信不疑}。
ctx.en: The children believe without a doubt that Father Christmas exists.

ctx.s: 他对自己的判断{深信不疑}，谁劝都不听。
ctx.en: He is completely sure of his own judgement and won't listen to anyone.

ctx.s: 奶奶对这个偏方{深信不疑}，每天都按时喝。
ctx.en: Grandma has total faith in this folk remedy and drinks it at the same time every day.

ctx.s: “你怎么那么肯定他是无辜的？”“我了解他，对此{深信不疑}。”
ctx.en: "How can you be so sure he's innocent?" "I know him; I have no doubt about it."

ctx.s: 经过多次实验，他对这个结论{深信不疑}。
ctx.en: After many experiments, he had no doubt at all about this conclusion.

ctx.s: 他始终{深信不疑}：只要坚持下去，总会成功。
ctx.en: He firmly believed throughout that if he kept going, he would succeed in the end.

bad.s: 我{深信不疑}他会不会来，所以一直在等。
bad.en: (meant: I wasn't sure whether he would come)
bad.why: It expresses complete certainty, so it cannot frame an open question about whether he will come.

bad.s: 这个朋友很{深信不疑}，你可以放心。
bad.en: (meant: this friend is very trustworthy)
bad.why: It describes a person who believes, not a person who deserves trust; nor can it be modified by 'very'.

story.text: The phrase comes from the Confucian classic The Great Learning, which says that when the mind is not present, one looks but does not see, listens but does not hear, and eats but does not know the taste. There it describes inattention; today it usually means deliberately ignoring something one ought to deal with.

use.how: Predicate, often 对……视而不见: 老师对作弊视而不见。 Criticises ignoring a problem, a person or a fact that is plainly there.

near.diff: 置之不理 is leaving a request or matter unanswered; 视而不见 stresses pretending not to notice something in plain sight.

cue: Litter has been piling up by the office door for weeks; everyone walks past it every day as if it weren't there. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 地上那么多垃圾，大家却都{视而不见}。
ctx.en: There's so much rubbish on the floor, yet everyone acts as if they don't see it.

ctx.s: 孩子在学校被欺负，老师怎么能{视而不见}呢？
ctx.en: A child is being bullied at school: how can the teacher turn a blind eye?

ctx.s: 这些违规就发生在管理人员眼皮底下，他们却长期{视而不见}。
ctx.en: These violations happened right under the managers' noses, yet for years they turned a blind eye.

ctx.s: “他又迟到了。”“经理好像一直{视而不见}。”
ctx.en: "He's late again." "The manager always seems to look the other way."

ctx.s: 对自己的缺点{视而不见}，是很难进步的。
ctx.en: If you ignore your own faults, it's very hard to improve.

ctx.s: 他找了半天钥匙，其实钥匙就在桌上，他却{视而不见}。
ctx.en: He searched for his keys for ages, though they were right on the table; he just looked straight past them.

bad.s: 天太黑了，我{视而不见}前面的路。
bad.en: (meant: it was too dark for me to see the road ahead)
bad.why: It is about ignoring what can be seen, not about being unable to see in the dark; use 'cannot see' instead.

bad.s: 他对朋友的成功{视而不见}，真是一个谦虚的人。
bad.en: (meant: he is modest about his friend's success)
bad.why: It is criticism for ignoring something one should notice; it cannot be used to praise modesty.

lit: to ruin oneself and abandon oneself

story.text: Mencius said that one cannot reason with those who ruin themselves, nor do anything worthwhile with those who abandon themselves. To speak against propriety and righteousness he called ruining oneself; to say 'I cannot live by benevolence and righteousness' he called abandoning oneself.

use.how: Predicate, very often after 不要 or 开始: 别因为一次失败就自暴自弃。 Said of a person who stops trying and lets themselves go, usually after a setback.

near.diff: 破罐破摔 is colloquial and blunter, making things worse on purpose since they are already bad; 自暴自弃 is neutral to formal, losing hope in oneself.

cue: After failing the entrance exam, a boy stops studying, sleeps all day and says he is worthless anyway. What is his friend warning him against?

ctx.s: 一次考试没考好，不要{自暴自弃}。
ctx.en: You did badly in one exam: don't give up on yourself.

ctx.s: 失业以后，他开始{自暴自弃}，整天喝酒。
ctx.en: After losing his job he gave up on himself and drank all day.

ctx.s: “我什么都做不好。”“别这么说，你可不能{自暴自弃}啊！”
ctx.en: "I can't do anything right." "Don't say that, you mustn't give up on yourself!"

ctx.s: 受伤后的那段日子，她差点{自暴自弃}，是家人把她拉了回来。
ctx.en: In the months after her injury she nearly gave up on herself; her family pulled her back.

ctx.s: 面对挫折，有人奋起，有人{自暴自弃}。
ctx.en: Faced with setbacks, some people rise up and others give up on themselves.

ctx.s: 老师相信，只要他不{自暴自弃}，一定还有机会。
ctx.en: The teacher believes that as long as he doesn't give up on himself, he still has a chance.

bad.s: 天气太热，我们{自暴自弃}了爬山的计划。
bad.en: (meant: we gave up our hiking plan because of the heat)
bad.why: It means losing hope in oneself, not dropping a plan, and it takes no object such as a plan.

bad.s: 他为了救别人，{自暴自弃}地冲进了火里。
bad.en: (meant: he selflessly rushed into the fire to save others)
bad.why: It is a criticism of despair and self-neglect, not a praise word for selfless courage.

mean: to rely on one's own efforts
lit: by one's own strength, to start life anew

use.how: Predicate or modifier: 我们要自力更生。 Said of a person, family, company or country that supports itself instead of depending on others' help.

near.diff: 白手起家 is building wealth or a business from nothing; 自力更生 is supporting oneself without outside help, with or without success.

cue: A village that used to live on government aid now grows and sells its own produce and needs no outside help. How do they live?

ctx.s: 他十八岁就离开家，开始{自力更生}。
ctx.en: He left home at eighteen and began supporting himself.

ctx.s: 父母年纪大了，我们得学会{自力更生}。
ctx.en: Our parents are getting old; we have to learn to stand on our own feet.

ctx.s: 这个村子不再依靠救济，靠种茶{自力更生}。
ctx.en: The village no longer depends on handouts; it supports itself by growing tea.

ctx.s: “毕业后还要家里给钱吗？”“不用，我想{自力更生}。”
ctx.en: "Will you still need money from home after graduating?" "No, I want to make it on my own."

ctx.s: 关键技术买不来，只能{自力更生}，自己研发。
ctx.en: Key technology can't be bought; we have to rely on ourselves and develop it.

ctx.s: 残疾以后，他没有依赖别人，而是学了一门手艺，{自力更生}。
ctx.en: After becoming disabled he didn't depend on others; he learned a trade and supported himself.

bad.s: 这道题太难了，我请老师帮我{自力更生}。
bad.en: (meant: I asked the teacher to help me work it out)
bad.why: It means doing without others' help; asking someone for help contradicts it.

bad.s: 这棵树枯了一冬，春天又{自力更生}了。
bad.en: (meant: the tree revived in spring)
bad.why: It is said of people, families or countries supporting themselves, not of a plant coming back to life.

lit: from the beginning to the end

use.how: Adverbial before the verb, often with 都 or 一直: 他自始至终都没说话。 Stresses that something held through a whole event or process without change.

near.diff: 始终如一 praises staying the same over a long time; 自始至终 simply marks the whole span of one event, often with 都.

cue: At a two-hour meeting, one person never said a single word, from the moment it opened until it closed. How long was he silent?

ctx.s: 开会的时候，他{自始至终}没说一句话。
ctx.en: He didn't say a word from the start of the meeting to the end.

ctx.s: 这场比赛{自始至终}都很精彩。
ctx.en: The match was exciting from beginning to end.

ctx.s: “你相信他吗？”“我{自始至终}都相信他。”
ctx.en: "Do you believe him?" "I've believed him all along."

ctx.s: 整个项目她{自始至终}都参与了，最了解情况。
ctx.en: She was involved in the whole project from start to finish, so she knows it best.

ctx.s: 手术进行了六个小时，医生{自始至终}保持着冷静。
ctx.en: The operation lasted six hours, and the surgeon stayed calm throughout.

ctx.s: 这部小说{自始至终}围绕着一个家庭展开。
ctx.en: From first page to last, the novel revolves around one family.

bad.s: 我{自始至终}去过北京三次。
bad.en: (meant: I have been to Beijing three times in total)
bad.why: It marks the whole span of one event, not a total count of repeated trips.

bad.s: 他从早上{自始至终}工作到晚上。
bad.en: (meant: he worked from morning to night)
bad.why: It already means 'from start to end', so adding a separate 'from morning to night' frame is redundant and ungrammatical.

lit: there will be a morning, one day

use.how: At the start of a clause, about an uncertain future day: 有朝一日我要去看看。 Often a hope or ambition, sometimes a warning; not for a fixed date.

near.diff: 总有一天 insists that the day will surely come; 有朝一日 is softer, a day that may come, often hoped for.

cue: A poor student dreams aloud of standing on a big stage as a famous singer, though she has no idea when or how. How does she start her sentence?

ctx.s: {有朝一日}，我一定要去西藏看看。
ctx.en: One day I'm definitely going to visit Tibet.

ctx.s: 他从小就梦想{有朝一日}能当上宇航员。
ctx.en: Since he was little he has dreamed of one day becoming an astronaut.

ctx.s: “你想过回老家吗？”“想过，{有朝一日}会回去的。”
ctx.en: "Have you thought of moving back to your hometown?" "I have; some day I'll go back."

ctx.s: 今天你这样对待别人，{有朝一日}别人也会这样对待你。
ctx.en: If you treat people like this today, some day they'll treat you the same way.

ctx.s: 科学家们希望，{有朝一日}这种病能够被彻底治愈。
ctx.en: Scientists hope this disease can one day be completely cured.

ctx.s: 临别时他说：“{有朝一日}我们还会再见面的。”
ctx.en: As they parted he said, "Some day we'll meet again."

bad.s: 我们{有朝一日}下午三点见面吧。
bad.en: (meant: let's meet at three o'clock one afternoon)
bad.why: It refers to an uncertain future, so it cannot go with a set time or appointment.

bad.s: 我{有朝一日}去过一次上海。
bad.en: (meant: I once went to Shanghai)
bad.why: It looks to the future; it cannot describe a trip that already happened.

mean: pleasing to the eye and mind
lit: delighting the heart and pleasing the eyes

use.how: Predicate or modifier, often 让人赏心悦目 or 赏心悦目的: 风景赏心悦目。 Said of scenery, design, handwriting or a performance that is pleasant to look at.

near.diff: 引人注目 means something stands out and draws attention, good or bad; 赏心悦目 means it is pleasant and soothing to look at.

cue: You open a friend's notebook: neat handwriting, soft colours, tidy margins. Just looking at it puts you in a good mood. How would you praise it?

ctx.s: 湖边的风景真是{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: The scenery by the lake is a real pleasure to look at.

ctx.s: 她的字写得工工整整，让人看了{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: Her handwriting is so neat that it's a joy to look at.

ctx.s: 这家餐厅的菜不但好吃，摆盘也{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: This restaurant's food is not only tasty, the plating is lovely to look at too.

ctx.s: “新网页怎么样？”“颜色很舒服，看着挺{赏心悦目}的。”
ctx.en: "How's the new website?" "The colours are easy on the eye; it's really pleasant to look at."

ctx.s: 春天的公园里，花开满园，令人{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: In spring the park is full of flowers, a delight to the eye.

ctx.s: 两位舞者配合默契，动作优美，{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: The two dancers moved in perfect harmony, graceful and a delight to watch.

bad.s: 听到这个好消息，他{赏心悦目}，高兴得跳了起来。
bad.en: (meant: hearing the good news, he was overjoyed and jumped for joy)
bad.why: It describes a sight that is pleasant to look at, not a person's own joy at hearing news.

bad.s: 车祸现场非常{赏心悦目}，很多人围着看。
bad.en: (meant: the accident scene drew a crowd of onlookers)
bad.why: It is praise for a pleasant sight; an accident scene may draw attention but is no pleasure to look at.

lit: to draw people's eyes to fix on it

use.how: Predicate or modifier: 一个引人注目的变化。 Said of a person, object, event or result that stands out and gets noticed, for good or ill.

near.diff: 赏心悦目 is about being pleasing to look at; 引人注目 is about standing out and being noticed, even for bad reasons.
引人入胜 is drawing someone deep into a story or scene; 引人注目 is only catching the eye and being noticed.

cue: In a hall full of people in grey suits, one guest walks in wearing a bright yellow coat, and every head turns. How would you describe her?

ctx.s: 她穿了一条红裙子，在人群中特别{引人注目}。
ctx.en: She wore a red dress and really stood out in the crowd.

ctx.s: 这座新建的大楼造型奇特，十分{引人注目}。
ctx.en: The new building has an unusual shape and catches everyone's eye.

ctx.s: “我们低调一点吧，别太{引人注目}。”
ctx.en: "Let's keep a low profile; we don't want to draw attention."

ctx.s: 今年最{引人注目}的变化，是年轻人越来越喜欢国货。
ctx.en: The most striking change this year is that young people increasingly like home-grown brands.

ctx.s: 这位新人在比赛中表现出色，成绩{引人注目}。
ctx.en: The newcomer did brilliantly in the competition, with results that turned heads.

ctx.s: 新闻里那张照片很{引人注目}，转发的人特别多。
ctx.en: That photo in the news drew a lot of attention, and huge numbers of people shared it.

bad.s: 我{引人注目}地听老师讲课。
bad.en: (meant: I listened attentively to the teacher)
bad.why: It describes something that draws others' attention, not a listener paying close attention.

bad.s: 这本小说太{引人注目}了，我一口气读完了。
bad.en: (meant: the novel was so gripping I read it in one go)
bad.why: It is about standing out to be noticed, not about a story absorbing you as you read.

lit: to lead people into a wonderful place

story.text: The phrase is traced to an anecdote in A New Account of Tales of the World: a Jin dynasty official known as General Wang is recorded as saying that wine truly leads a person into a wonderful place. The 'wonderful place' later came to mean the absorbing heart of a story, a landscape or a work of art.

use.how: Predicate or modifier: 情节引人入胜。 Said of a story, film, book, talk or scenery that draws you deeper and holds you there.

near.diff: 引人注目 is catching the eye at first sight; 引人入胜 is pulling the reader or viewer in and keeping them absorbed.

cue: You meant to read one chapter before bed, but the plot kept pulling you deeper, and suddenly it was three in the morning. How was the book?

ctx.s: 这部电影的情节{引人入胜}，一点也不无聊。
ctx.en: The film's plot is gripping; not boring at all.

ctx.s: 他讲历史故事讲得{引人入胜}，学生们都听入迷了。
ctx.en: He tells history stories so enthrallingly that the students are spellbound.

ctx.s: “这本书好看吗？”“开头就{引人入胜}，我停不下来。”
ctx.en: "Is the book good?" "It draws you in from the start; I couldn't put it down."

ctx.s: 山路越走越深，景色也越来越{引人入胜}。
ctx.en: The deeper the mountain path went, the more enchanting the scenery became.

ctx.s: 一篇好的开头，应该{引人入胜}，让读者想继续读下去。
ctx.en: A good opening should draw readers in and make them want to keep reading.

ctx.s: 这个纪录片用一个个真实的人物，讲述了一段{引人入胜}的历史。
ctx.en: Through a series of real people, the documentary tells an absorbing piece of history.

bad.s: 她的新发型很{引人入胜}，大家都多看了两眼。
bad.en: (meant: her new hairstyle caught everyone's eye)
bad.why: It is about being drawn deeper into a story or scene; a hairstyle simply catches the eye and has nothing to draw you into.

bad.s: 这个菜的味道{引人入胜}，我吃了两碗饭。
bad.en: (meant: this dish tastes wonderful)
bad.why: It is used for stories, works and scenery that absorb you, not for the taste of food.
